title: What's new in Swift 6.2 to 6.4
summary: Swift 6.2 made concurrency easier (main actor by default, async functions run where they are called, `@concurrent` to go to the background) and added `InlineArray`, `Span` and `Observations`. 6.3/6.4 continue with ergonomics and diagnostics.
body: **Swift 6.2 (Sept 2025) in simple words:** before, Swift 6 strict concurrency produced lots of errors in UI code. 6.2 lets a module say "everything is on the main actor unless I say otherwise" (`defaultIsolation(MainActor.self)`). Plain async functions now run on the caller's actor (no surprise thread hop); mark CPU-heavy ones `@concurrent` to run in the background.

**Other 6.2 items:** isolated conformances (`extension Model: @MainActor Equatable`), `Task.immediate`, task names visible in Instruments, `weak let`, `InlineArray` and `Span`, `Observations` async sequence for `@Observable` models, Swift Testing exit tests and attachments, opt-in strict memory safety mode.
**Swift 6.1:** `nonisolated` on types/extensions, trailing commas in more places, package traits.

**Swift 6.3/6.4 (2026, WWDC26):** reported changes include async calls inside `defer`, warnings when a task silently drops a thrown error, an `anyAppleOS` availability shorthand, and more ownership and diagnostics work. Verify details against the official release notes before quoting them.

**How to talk about it:** interviewers care about impact - why default main-actor isolation reduces migration noise, when `@concurrent` is needed, and what behavior changes when upcoming feature flags are turned on.
keyPoints: 6.2: default MainActor isolation per module; caller-isolated async functions; `@concurrent` to offload.
Turning on `NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault` can move work onto main - profile and add `@concurrent`.
Talk about adoption impact, not just feature lists.

followups: **What breaks when enabling `NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault`?** Async functions that relied on leaving the main actor now run on it; heavy work may cause hangs until marked `@concurrent`.
